A1.evidence: The code is retrievable over HTTPS from https://zenodo.org/records/10623550 (p. 3) and through DOI resolution. The pack shows access_right 'open'.

A1_1.evidence: HTTPS and DOI/Handle resolution are open, free, and universally implementable. The Zenodo API resolved with HTTP 200.

A1_2.evidence: The code is fully open with no authentication required (pack access_right: 'open'), which satisfies A1.2 under the v2.1 open case. No restriction is warranted.

A2.evidence: Rung (i) is silent on persistence. Under rung (ii), Zenodo (Row 2) retains a tombstone page with DOI and URL on withdrawal and keeps metadata always publicly accessible. The DataCite DOI (Row 1) is undeletable and Handle-resolvable.

F1.evidence: Principal code: the authors' 'Dedicated R code' (Supplementary Information S2/S3), deposited with the data: 'All code and data are available here: https://zenodo.org/records/10623550' (p. 3). The deposit has its own DataCite DOI, 10.5281/zenodo.10623550 (pack; Zenodo resource_type 'dataset', concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10623549).

F2.evidence: The deposit has an independent artefact-level metadata record (pack metadata_record: true at DataCite and Zenodo; structured fields: publisher, publication_year, resource_type, licence). The instrument operationalises F2 as an independent metadata record for own-PID deposits. Description and keywords are not itemised in the pack.

F3.evidence: The pack shows identifier_in_metadata: true for 10.5281/zenodo.10623550 at both the DataCite and Zenodo endpoints.

F4.evidence: The deposit is indexed in DataCite (state 'findable') and in the Zenodo record index (record 10623550, HTTP 200).

I1.evidence: The code is written in R, an open, formal, widely shared language: 'All analyses were performed in the open-source R programming environment (v.4.2.2...)' (p. 3). The deposit metadata are DataCite-schema structured records (pack).

I2.evidence: No FAIR vocabularies are evidenced for the software: no CodeMeta, no controlled software or dependency vocabulary, and no PID-bearing terms. The pack and platform table are silent, so the ladder is exhausted.

I3.evidence: Through dependency citation quality (aggregation rule), the key third-party dependency is cited with a qualified PID reference: 'using the Quanteda package (Benoit et al., 2018)' (p. 3), with reference 'quanteda: an R package for the quantitative analysis of textual data. JOSS 3, 774. https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.00774' (p. 8). R is cited by version (v.4.2.2) as 'R Core Team, 2021', with no URL or PID; R has no conventional PID.

R1.evidence: The paper specifies the analysis in detail. It gives the k-skip-n-gram design with 'the k value for all generated skipgrams is thus set to 13', justified by a maximum of 15 motifs per object (p. 3). It sets n = 2, 3, 4 and gives the expected-frequency and PMI formulas (p. 3). It specifies alphabetical ordering of motif strings (pp. 2-3), the Table 2 exclusion rule ('Cooccurrences with observed values below three are excluded'), and the software and version (R v.4.2.2, Quanteda). Deposit README contents are not evidenced (supplements not provided).

R1_1.evidence: The paper is silent on the code licence. Per R1.1, the licence recorded at the service governs: the pack shows cc-by-4.0 for the deposit at both DataCite and Zenodo, with no conflicts. CC-BY-4.0 is an identified licence (a Zenodo default value is fully operative).

R1_2.evidence: Code provenance is documented. The authors are identified, with CRediT for Herskind: 'Methodology, Investigation, Formal analysis, Data curation' (p. 8). The runtime is 'R programming environment (v.4.2.2...)' with the Quanteda package (p. 3), and the input data lineage and transformations are described (pp. 2-3). Gap: no Quanteda version is given.

R1_3.evidence: The deposit qualifies under route (a), generic metadata schemas: the code is described by a DataCite Metadata Schema record (pack, state 'findable'). No code-specific standard (package structure, CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, CRAN, JOSS, or rOpenSci review) is evidenced for the authors' scripts. Quanteda's JOSS review is a dependency's credential and cannot substitute for the principal scripts.

barriers: Upstream source Płonka (2003), The Portable Art of Mesolithic Europe, is an analogue printed monograph (closed/paywalled monograph barrier). Paper p. 2: 'From this analogue compilation, the South Scandinavian data were manually extracted and digitised'. The paper also states that all 483 South Scandinavian object records it uses, with Płonka's motif coding and metadata, are deposited openly ('complete data tables', 'All code and data are available here: https://zenodo.org/records/10623550'). The upstream records the analysis needs are therefore counted as accessible at Tier 0 through the authors' redistribution. The monograph itself is needed only to verify the manual transcription, not to reproduce the reported results. Record-weighted coverage is 483/483 = 100%. Counting the analogue volume as a separate Tier-3 dataset would count the same 483 records twice.

Two Zenodo versions are cited under one concept DOI (10.5281/zenodo.10623549): the Methods cite record 10623550 and the data availability statement cites record 10801706. Both are open, so this is a version-citation inconsistency, not an access barrier.
Supplementary files were deliberately not provided to the assessor, so completeness rests on the paper's own statements ('complete data tables'; 'All code and data').

A1.evidence: The full research dataset is retrievable over HTTPS from Zenodo via DOI or record URL. The paper says 'complete data tables are reported in Supplementary Information S2 and S3... All code and data are available here: https://zenodo.org/records/10623550' (p. 3), and the pack shows access_right: open. Data-completeness coverage is complete (100%; record-weighted 483/483). The only upstream source, the analogue Płonka (2003) catalogue, has its required records redistributed in the deposit, so the A1 completeness override does not apply.

A1_1.evidence: Retrieval uses HTTPS (zenodo.org record URLs cited on pp. 3 and 8) and DOI/Handle resolution, which are open, free, and universally implementable protocols. The pack shows access_right 'open' and resolving API requests (HTTP 200).

A1_2.evidence: This is a fully open resource requiring no authentication (pack access_right: 'open'), which satisfies A1.2 under the v2.1 open case. No access control is warranted: the data are a transcription of a published catalogue, not sensitive data.

A2.evidence: Rung (i) is silent on metadata persistence, so this rests on rung (ii). Zenodo (Row 2) provides a tombstone page on withdrawal with DOI and URL retained, and its metadata is always publicly accessible (platform policy assertion). The DataCite DOI (Row 1) is undeletable. The pack confirms Zenodo hosting and DataCite registration.

F1.evidence: Principal dataset: the author-digitised corpus of 483 South Scandinavian Mesolithic ornamented objects, with Płonka motif presence/absence coding and metadata. It is deposited on Zenodo with its own DataCite DOIs: 10.5281/zenodo.10623550 (p. 3, 'All code and data are available here: https://zenodo.org/records/10623550') and 10.5281/zenodo.10801706 (data availability statement, p. 8), both under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10623549. The paper cites Zenodo record URLs; the pack confirms the corresponding DOIs (state 'findable'). Both versions carry their own PID, so the conjunctive scoring holds. The publisher-hosted Appendix A supplement is not principal, because the Zenodo deposit holds all code and data.

F2.evidence: Each version has an independent artefact-level metadata record. The pack shows metadata_record: true at both DataCite and Zenodo, with structured fields (publisher 'Zenodo', publication_year 2024, resource_type 'Dataset', licence, state). The instrument's F1 note operationalises F2 as an independent metadata record, giving F 4/4 for an own-PID deposit. Note: the pack does not itemise description or keywords, and Zenodo Row 2 does not guarantee a description.

F3.evidence: The pack records identifier_in_metadata: true for both Zenodo versions at both the DataCite and Zenodo endpoints.

F4.evidence: Both versions are registered and indexed in DataCite (pack: DataCite API resolved, state 'findable') and in the Zenodo record index (Zenodo API resolved, record ids 10623550 and 10801706).

I1.evidence: The metadata use a formal, shared representation: DataCite Metadata Schema records served as structured data by the DataCite and Zenodo APIs (pack: resolved structured records with typed fields). The paper describes the data as structured tabular coding ('transcribed as binary data in the form of presence/absence coding', 'complete data tables', p. 2-3) that the deposited R code processes. Note: the file formats are not stated in the paper or the pack.

I2.evidence: No FAIR vocabulary is evidenced. Motifs are coded with Płonka's own typology labels ('motif types (named A1, A2, etc.)', p. 2), which have no PIDs. Chronology uses culture-historical names (Maglemose, Kongemose, Ertebølle) with no PeriodO or similar URIs. Artefact types and places are not linked to Getty AAT, a gazetteer, or similar vocabularies. The pack shows no vocabulary information and no platform-table row entitles this, so the ladder is exhausted.

I3.evidence: No qualified PID references from the data to other resources are evidenced. The upstream source, Płonka (2003), is cited only bibliographically and has no PID; objects are cross-referenced by 'Figure in Płonka (2003)' numbers (Table 3), not PIDs. The pack records no relatedIdentifiers (for example, to the article DOI). The only PID linkage shown is Zenodo's concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10623549, a versioning self-link to the same deposit rather than a reference to another resource. No table entitlement applies.

R1.evidence: The paper describes the dataset with many attributes: 483 objects (S1); 'numerous categorical variables corresponding to the characteristics of each ornamented object and associated metadata such as location, quality of contextual information, and original source' (p. 2); Płonka's motif scheme (pp. 315-325) coded as presence/absence; transformation into alphabetically ordered 'sentence' strings (pp. 2-3); and 'pertinent metadata such as artefact classes, chronology, and spatial distribution' (p. 7). Table 1 summarises frequencies.

R1_1.evidence: The paper is silent on the deposit's licence (the article's CC BY licence covers the article, a separate artefact). Under the R1.1 rule the deposit is scored on the licence recorded at the service. The pack shows cc-by-4.0 for both Zenodo versions at both DataCite and Zenodo, with no licence conflicts, so the licence is identified (CC-BY-4.0).

R1_2.evidence: Provenance is detailed. The source is 'the comprehensive catalogue of Mesolithic ornamentation compiled by Płonka (2003). From this analogue compilation, the South Scandinavian data were manually extracted and digitised' (p. 2). The motif scheme is from Płonka pp. 315-325. The transformation steps (presence/absence, then sentence strings) and the processing software (R v.4.2.2, Quanteda) are stated on p. 3. Per-object source figures appear in Table 3. CRediT records Herskind: 'Data curation' (p. 8).

R1_3.evidence: This qualifies under route (a), generic metadata schemas. The pack shows both Zenodo versions are described by DataCite Metadata Schema records registered at DataCite (state 'findable', resource_type 'Dataset'). No domain standard (ARIADNEplus, CIDOC-CRM) and no accredited domain repository is evidenced. The methodological standards (skipgram/PMI, Płonka typology) do not qualify.
